subtitle: How a Midnight Pact in Murshidabad Opened the Gates of Empire

panels.shot: split-panel composition, one half showing Robert Clive in red coat over a map of Bengal, the other half Siraj ud-Daulah on a palace terrace, both looming over a misty battlefield with cannons
panels.action: Robert Clive stands over a parchment treaty and scattered gold coins, eyes calculating, while Siraj ud-Daulah grips the hilt of his sword on a Murshidabad balcony, the distant plain of Palashi and lined-up armies fading into stormy clouds below.

dialogue.text: Before the guns spoke at Plassey in 1757, the fate of Bengal had already been written in ink and whispers, by Robert Clive, Siraj ud-Daulah, and a quiet general named Mir Jafar.

i18n.hi: १७५७ की प्लासी की तोपें गरजीं, पर बंगाल की किस्मत पहले ही कलम, फुसफुसाहट और रॉबर्ट क्लाइव, सिराजउद्दौला और खामोश सरदार मीर जाफर ने लिख दी थी।

panels.shot: wide aerial shot of the Hooghly River and Calcutta settlement, with Fort William small against the vast delta
panels.action: A humid dawn over the Hooghly shows the fragile English settlement of Calcutta huddled along the riverbank, Fort William’s walls thin against the sprawling, misty Bengal landscape and the distant outline of Murshidabad’s wealth.

dialogue.text: In the mid-eighteenth century, Bengal was one of the richest provinces of the Mughal world, and a foreign trading company from a cold island clung to the riverbanks at Calcutta behind Fort William’s slender walls.

i18n.hi: अठारहवीं सदी के बीचोंबीच, बंगाल मुगल दुनिया का सबसे अमीर सूबों में था, और दूर की ठंडी टापू की एक फिरंगी कम्पनी कलकत्ता की नदी किनारे फ़ोर्ट विलियम की पतली दीवारों के पीछे चिपकी बैठी थी।

panels.shot: medium split shot, Siraj in durbar on one side, Clive on a ship deck on the other
panels.action: On one side, a youthful Siraj ud-Daulah sits in formal durbar at Murshidabad, face set but restless amid courtiers and jewel-laden pillars; on the other, Robert Clive stands on a ship deck approaching Bengal, coat whipping in the river wind.

dialogue.text: Alivardi Khan’s chosen heir, Siraj ud-Daulah, came to the masnad in 1756 amid suspicion and intrigue. From the sea, Robert Clive, soldier and clerk turned adventurer, sailed back to Bengal with Company troops and unfinished grudges.

i18n.hi: अलीवर्दी ख़ान के मनचाहे वारिस सिराजउद्दौला १७५६ में शक और साज़िशों के बीच मसंद पर बैठे। समंदर से क्लर्क से सिपाही बना मुहिमबाज़ रॉबर्ट क्लाइव कम्पनी की फौज और अपने अधूरे बदले लेकर लौट पड़ा।

panels.shot: low-angle interior durbar shot focused on Siraj, with angry merchants and letters piled before him
panels.action: Siraj ud-Daulah leans forward on his throne, brows furrowed, as petitions about English fortifications and minting rights lie piled before him; behind, merchants and officers murmur about the Company’s growing defiance.

dialogue.text: Siraj inherited a province where European companies fortified without leave, coined money under Mughal name yet claimed their own power, and sheltered his enemies in Calcutta. He chose to assert authority rather than yield it.

i18n.hi: सिराज को ऐसा सूबा मिला जहाँ यूरोपीय कंपनियाँ बिना इजाज़त किले उठातीं, मुगल नाम से सिक्के ढालतीं पर ताकत अपनी मानतीं, और उसके दुश्मनों को कलकत्ता में पनाह देतीं। उसने झुकने के बजाय हुकूमत दिखाने का रास्ता चुना।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of Nawab’s army before Fort William, with stormy sky
panels.action: Under a brooding monsoon sky, Siraj’s standards and elephants stand before the battered walls of Fort William, cannons poised; smoke and confusion hang over the English settlement as native inhabitants scatter along muddy streets.

dialogue.text: In 1756, Siraj marched on Calcutta. Fort William fell, the English fled to the river, and later accounts by John Holwell told a grim tale of a crowded prison night that would echo in London, though its exact toll remains disputed.

i18n.hi: १७५६ में सिराज कलकत्ता पर चढ़ आया। फ़ोर्ट विलियम गिरा, अँग्रेज़ नदी की ओर भागे, और जॉन हॉवेल की लिखी भरी कोठरी वाली रात की कहानी लंदन तक गूँजी, चाहे आज भी उसके मारे गए लोगों की गिनती पर झगड़ा हो।

panels.shot: tight interior on Clive in council tent aboard ship, candlelit maps of Bengal spread out
panels.action: By candlelight in a crowded ship’s cabin, Robert Clive bends over a map of Bengal, officers around him tense; he points toward Calcutta and then inland, while the flicker of the flame makes the river lines seem to twist like snakes.

dialogue.text: The Company’s answer came swift. Clive recaptured Calcutta with naval support, struck at Chandernagore, and then gazed upriver toward Murshidabad, where the Nawab sat surrounded by discontented grandees.

i18n.hi: कम्पनी का जवाब बिजली जैसा आया। क्लाइव ने बेड़े की मदद से कलकत्ता वापस लिया, चंद्रनगर पर वार किया, और फिर नज़र उठाकर मुर्शिदाबाद की ओर देखी, जहाँ नवाब नाराज़ उमरावों से घिरा बैठा था।

panels.shot: shadowy interior of a noble’s mansion in Murshidabad, conspirators in semi-silhouette
panels.action: In a lamplit chamber of a Murshidabad mansion, Mir Jafar and other disaffected nobles huddle in quiet conversation, faces half in shadow, a folded Persian letter from the English lying untouched between them.

dialogue.text: Within Siraj’s own court, men like Mir Jafar, his commander-in-chief, nursed wounded pride and hopes of the masnad. To them the Company now extended not cannon first, but ink, promises, and gold.

i18n.hi: सिराज के ही दरबार में उसके सेनापति-ए-आला मीर जाफर जैसे लोग ज़ख्मी अहं और मसंद की उम्मीदें पाल रहे थे। इन्हीं तक कम्पनी ने अब तोप नहीं, कलम, वादे और सोना बढ़ाया।

panels.shot: close-up on hands exchanging a Persian treaty document over a low table
panels.action: Two unseen figures’ hands meet over a low carpeted table, one pale, one dark, as a freshly written Persian treaty sheet is exchanged; beside it lie small bars of silver and a rough sketch of Murshidabad’s palace.

dialogue.text: The Clive–Mir Jafar agreement promised the general the nawabship if he and his allies stood aside, rich jagirs and payments to the Company if its arms prevailed, and a new order where trade would be secured by treason as much as by steel.

i18n.hi: क्लाइव–मीर जाफर समझौते में वादा था: अगर वह और उसके साथी हटकर खड़े रहें तो उसे नवाबी, कम्पनी को जीत पर मोटी जागीरें और नक़द, और ऐसा नया निज़ाम जहाँ व्यापार तलवार जितना ग़द्दारी से भी सुरक्षित हो।

panels.shot: medium shot of Clive with two parchments, one in each hand, in a dim room
panels.action: In a dim chamber, Robert Clive holds two nearly identical Persian parchments, one bearing Omichand’s promised reward and one stripped of it, his face impassive as an Indian intermediary watches with a troubled gaze.

dialogue.text: To win over the broker Omichand, the Company men resorted to double paper. One treaty, with rich promises for him; another, without. Clive would later admit in Parliament that the forged duplicate was deliberate deceit.

i18n.hi: दलाल ओमीचंद को फाँसने के लिए कम्पनी वालों ने दो काग़ज़ निकाले। एक संधि उस पर मीठे वादों के साथ, दूसरी बिना। क्लाइव ने बाद में पार्लियामेंट में मान लिया कि यह नकली नकल जानबूझकर की गई धोखेबाज़ी थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Siraj’s camp with astrologers and courtiers, evening before battle
panels.action: On the eve of battle at the village of Palashi, Siraj’s grand camp stretches along the Bhagirathi, tents glowing in lamplight; astrologers murmur, courtiers press him with conflicting counsel, and the young Nawab sits torn between pride and fear.

dialogue.speaker: robert_clive_and_siraj_ud_daulah
dialogue.text: “They are few, we are many. Yet whose hearts can I trust?”

i18n.hi: “वे थोड़े हैं, हम ज़्यादा। पर किस दिल पर मैं भरोसा करूँ?”

panels.shot: early-morning panoramic of opposing armies arrayed near mango grove at Plassey
panels.action: Under a pale dawn, Siraj’s vast army lines the open ground near a thick mango grove, cannons and war elephants arrayed, while across the field Clive’s smaller force, in disciplined ranks, positions itself near the trees’ shade.

dialogue.text: On 23 June 1757, at Palashi on the Bhagirathi, Siraj’s army outnumbered the Company’s by several times. Ghulam Hussain’s Siyar calls what followed an artificial battle, where treachery, not strength, proved decisive.

i18n.hi: २३ जून १७५७ को भागीरथी किनारे पलाशी में सिराज की फौज कम्पनी से कई गुना थी। ग़ुलाम हुसैन की ‘सियर’ इसे बनावटी जंग कहती है, जहाँ निर्णायक ताकत नहीं, दग़ा थी।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Mir Madan urging troops forward near cannon smoke
panels.action: Amid rolling cannon smoke, Mir Madan rides forward, arm outstretched, urging Bengal troops and artillery into action as their guns thunder toward the grove, while rain clouds gather heavily overhead.

dialogue.text: As the first hours passed, it was Mir Madan, one of Siraj’s truest officers, who pressed the attack. Clive’s own dispatches and later accounts agree: the Nawab’s side fought hard at the start.

i18n.hi: पहले पहरों में सिराज के सच्चे अफ़सरों में से एक मीर मदन ही था जिसने हमला दबाकर किया। क्लाइव की अपनी रिपोर्टें और बाद की कहानियाँ मानती हैं कि शुरुआत में नवाब की तरफ़ से लड़ाई सख़्त थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of sudden rain over the battlefield, artillery pieces being covered
panels.action: A sudden monsoon shower sweeps across the field, soaking powder and men alike; Bengal gunners scramble to cover their cannons with cloth, while in the mango grove Company troops shield their guns under tarpaulins, waiting.

dialogue.text: Then the rain came. On the open ground, Bengal’s artillery was hastily covered, its powder at risk. In the grove, Company cannons lay better protected, ready to fire again once the storm passed.

i18n.hi: फिर बारिश आई। खुले मैदान में बंगाल की तोपों को जल्दी-जल्दी ढका गया, बारूद भीगने को था। बाग़ की झाड़ियों में कम्पनी की तोपें ज़्यादा सुरक्षित थीं, तूफ़ान थमते ही फिर बरसने को तैयार।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mir Madan being carried away on a palanquin, troops around him faltering
panels.action: Under the dark sky, soldiers carry Mir Madan away on a palanquin, his body still; the nearby lines waver, men glancing anxiously toward the distant figures of Mir Jafar’s untouched troops.

dialogue.text: Amid the chaos, Mir Madan was struck down. With their fiercest officer gone and the rain’s confusion, Siraj’s camp looked toward Mir Jafar’s wings for relief. They saw only stillness.

i18n.hi: हंगामे में मीर मदन ढेर हो गया। सबसे तेज़ अफ़सर के गिरते ही और बारिश की अफ़रा-तफ़री में सिराज का डेरा मदद के लिए मीर जाफर के परों की तरफ़ देखने लगा। वहाँ बस ख़ामोशी थी।

panels.shot: long shot of Mir Jafar’s contingent standing motionless while others fight
panels.action: On a slight rise, Mir Jafar’s well-equipped troops stand in ordered ranks, banners unmoving, as distant explosions and musket fire continue; his face is unreadable as he watches the battle unfold without raising his hand.

dialogue.text: Mir Jafar’s divisions did not move. The man promised the throne kept his soldiers still while others bled. To Clive, this was the treaty taking form; to later chroniclers, it was the moment honour died.

i18n.hi: मीर जाफर की टुकड़ियाँ टस से मस न हुईं। जिस पर तख़्त का वादा था, उसने अपने सिपाहियों को जमे रहने दिया, जबकि औरों का ख़ून बहा। क्लाइव के लिए यह लिखी हुई डील का रूप था, और बाद के तारीख़-निगारों के लिए वही घड़ी थी जब मान गिर पड़ा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Clive in the grove ordering renewed fire, resolute expression
panels.action: From within the mango grove, Robert Clive, coat damp but face firm, signals his gunners and infantry to advance and renew their fire, as the smoke now rolls toward a wavering Bengal line deprived of support.

dialogue.text: Seeing the enemy’s confusion and their silent allies, Clive pushed forward. In his letters he told London of a hard-won field, but even he knew the day was as much won by prior promises as by shot.

i18n.hi: दुश्मन की घबराहट और अपने खामोश साथियों को देखकर क्लाइव आगे बढ़ा। अपने ख़तों में उसने लंदन को सख़्त जीती हुई जंग लिखी, पर भीतर जानता था कि यह दिन तो उतना ही पहले के वादों से जीता गया, जितना गोले से।

panels.shot: intimate shot inside Siraj’s command tent as news of defections arrives
panels.action: Inside a richly furnished tent, Siraj ud-Daulah stands half-risen from his seat, face drained, as a messenger kneels with news of broken lines and silent commanders; maps and jewels lie scattered, a symbol of power slipping away.

dialogue.speaker: robert_clive_and_siraj_ud_daulah
dialogue.text: “The field betrays me. The court will not spare me.”

i18n.hi: “मैदान ने साथ छोड़ा, दरबार जान बख़्शेगा नहीं।”

panels.shot: wide dusk shot of Siraj’s small escort fleeing in boats across the river
panels.action: As dusk gathers, Siraj ud-Daulah, no longer in ceremonial robes, boards a small boat with a few loyal attendants, pushing away from the riverbank while smoke from the battlefield drifts behind him along the Bhagirathi.

dialogue.text: With his lines collapsing and his commanders divided, Siraj fled toward Murshidabad. The Siyar would later portray his end as the product of courtly betrayal and foreign greed more than of single-day cowardice.

i18n.hi: सफ़ें टूटती, सरदार टूटते देख सिराज मुर्शिदाबाद की ओर भागा। ‘सियर’ में उसका अंजाम ज़्यादा दरबारी धोखे और पराये लालच का नतीजा दिखता है, न कि सिर्फ़ एक दिन की डरपोक़ी का।

panels.shot: interior palace shot of Mir Jafar being seated on Nawab’s throne as Clive watches
panels.action: In the great hall of Murshidabad, Mir Jafar is ceremonially seated on the Nawab’s throne, courtiers bowing, while Robert Clive stands to one side in his red coat, observing the scene with a cool, satisfied gaze.

dialogue.text: Soon after, Siraj was captured and killed by his enemies in the court, and Mir Jafar was raised as Nawab. Ghulam Hussain records this as a triumph built on perfidy, a change of master rather than a rescue of Bengal.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही सिराज दरबार के दुश्मनों के हाथ लगा और मारा गया, और मीर जाफर नवाब बना उठाया गया। ग़ुलाम हुसैन इसे दग़ेबाज़ी पर खड़ी फ़तह लिखता है, मालिक की अदला-बदली, न कि बंगाल की मुक्ति।

panels.shot: close-up of chests of coins and jewels being weighed, Clive in background
panels.action: Heavy wooden chests of coins and jewels are prised open and weighed in a Murshidabad courtyard; in the background, Clive stands with Company officials, scribes recording sums as Indian treasurers look on uneasily.

dialogue.text: From Mir Jafar came vast payments to the Company and its servants. Records show Clive himself received a personal fortune, around £234,000, even as British historians would long remember him chiefly as a daring general.

i18n.hi: मीर जाफर से कम्पनी और उसके नौकरों को ख़ज़ाने की नदियाँ बहीं। रिकॉर्ड बताते हैं कि क्लाइव ने अकेले तकरीबन २३४,००० पाउंड की निजी दौलत समेटी, जबकि ब्रिटिश तारीख़ लंबे समय तक उसे बस दिलेर फ़ौजी ही कहती रही।

panels.shot: montage-style wide showing Company factors collecting revenue in Bengal countryside
panels.action: In the Bengal countryside, Company agents sit beneath a banyan tree with ledgers as local officials bring in bundles of revenue papers; peasants and zamindars stand in line, unsure of this new authority that writes in English and Persian both.

dialogue.text: The aftermath reached far beyond Palashi’s grove. Over the next years, Company influence over Bengal’s finances deepened, culminating in the diwani grant of 1765, when Mughal authority formally handed them the right to collect revenue.

i18n.hi: पलाशी के बाग़ से आगे तक तूफ़ान फैला। अगले सालों में कम्पनी का बंगाल के ख़ज़ाने पर हाथ गहराता गया, और १७६५ की दीवानी पर आकर थमा, जब मुगल बादशाह ने बाक़ायदा उन्हें वसूली का हक़ थमा दिया।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of an older Clive before a British parliamentary committee, documents in hand
panels.action: An older Robert Clive stands before a panel of British parliamentarians in London, stacks of Indian documents on the table, his face lined as he answers questions about treaties, fortunes, and the conduct of the Company in Bengal.

dialogue.text: Decades later, Clive would defend himself in Parliament, admitting the forged treaty and the riches he received, arguing that in a corrupt world he had taken no more than his due, while critics cited Plassey as the first step into dangerous power.

i18n.hi: कई दशकों बाद क्लाइव ने पार्लियामेंट में अपना बचाव किया, झूठी संधि और अपनी कमाई दोनों मानकर कहा कि सड़ी हुई दुनिया में उसने बस अपना हिस्सा लिया, जबकि उसके आलोचक प्लासी को ख़तरनाक सत्ता की पहली सीढ़ी बताते रहे।

panels.shot: reflective wide shot of the deserted mango grove at Plassey in calm daylight, no armies
panels.action: The mango grove at Palashi lies quiet now, trees casting soft shade over empty ground; the river glints in the distance, and in the mind’s eye faint images of Siraj, Clive, and Mir Jafar seem to fade among the trunks.

dialogue.text: Plassey was not only a battle, but a treaty, a gamble, and a betrayal. In that grove, a provincial succession crisis opened the way for Company rule, reminding us that some victories are signed long before they are fought.

i18n.hi: प्लासी सिर्फ़ जंग नहीं, एक संधि, एक दाँव और एक धोखा थी। उसी बाग़ में सूबे की उत्तराधिकार की खींचतान ने कम्पनी राज की राह खोली, याद दिलाते हुए कि कुछ फ़तहें तलवार से पहले काग़ज़ पर लिखी जाती हैं।

title_i18n.en: Plassey Was a Treaty Before a Battle
title_i18n.hi: प्लासी: जंग से पहले हुआ सौदा

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Midnight Pact in Murshidabad Opened the Gates of Empire
subtitle_i18n.hi: मुर्शिदाबाद की आधी रात की साज़िश से खुला साम्राज्य का दरवाज़ा
